The '''Baybay language''', also known as ''Baybayanon'', ''Utudnon'', ''Waya-Waya'' or ''Leyte'', is a distinct [[regional language]] that was spoken on the island of [[Leyte]] in the [[Philippines]] before the arrival of [[Waray language|Waray]] and then later, [[Boholano language|Boholano]] and [[Cebuano language|Cebuano]]. It is still spoken around the city of [[Baybay]]. It is part of the [[Bisayan languages|Bisayan language family]] and is closely related to other [[Philippine languages]].

==Classification==
Baybayanon was originally a Warayan language that has been [[relexified]] and overlaid by a [[Cebuano language|Cebuano]] (Leyteño) [[superstratum]].<ref name="Rubino 2005" /> The Warayan substratum is characterized by Baybayanon's more Waray-like [[deictic]]s, and various other features.<ref name="Rubino 2005" />

==Geographic distribution==
Utudnon is spoken by about 10,000 people in five [[barangay]]s of [[Baybay]] municipality,<ref>{{Cite web |last=ISO 639-3 Registration Authority  |date=2009 |title=Request for New Language Code Element in ISO 639-3 |url=http://www-01.sil.org/iso639-3/cr_files/2009-083_bvy.pdf |id=request number 2009-083}}</ref> central [[Leyte]], namely Utúd (also called Utod or Guadalupe), Gábas, Kilím, Pátag, Pangasúgan and Hibunawan.<ref name="Rubino 2005">{{Cite book |last=Rubino |first=Carl |chapter-url=https://www.sil.org/system/files/reapdata/11/14/06/111406141854006765272845103534076166535/Rubino.pdf |title=Current Issues in Philippine Linguistics and Anthropology: Parangal kay Lawrence A.
